research_question: Can transferable AI architecture gain be expressed as a multi-budget law g(P,R,V,M,W,E) with identifiable main effects, saturation/curvature, and cross-factor interactions?
primary_target: g = ln((1-baseline_score+0.001)/(1-intervention_score+0.001)) within the same model/task condition
stage_A: 2^5 full factorial OFF/HIGH; estimates every distinct-factor interaction R,V,M,W,E through order 5
stage_B: face-centered axial points + center/off/high replicates; estimates univariate curvature, saturation diagnostics, and pure error
outer_regimes: same architecture family at three active-parameter scales; same condition matrix repeated; hold out an entire model scale and an entire task regime
primary_candidate_families: multiplicative remaining-error law: g = sum beta_i z_i
pair interaction law: g = sum beta_i z_i + sum gamma_ij z_i z_j
all-order interaction expansion nominated adaptively by Atlas
saturation law: g = gmax(1-exp(-sum lambda_i z_i))
promotion_rule: No coefficient/exponent is called transferable unless its required design columns are full rank and it survives regime holdout plus whole-pipeline null.
open_endedness: Stage A/B is an execution design, not a scientific ceiling. Higher orders/axes may be added by the Atlas residual/frontier loop.
